expectations.text: Out-of-scope items of the target requirements are not designed or built
expectations.evidence: No recipe origin ('No origin is shown'), no line editing ('Lines are not editable'), add/delete/move/finish disabled offline, single list per household, fixed area enum. Nothing out-of-scope designed.

expectations.text: Data model given with entities, fields and types; API/interfaces given with method, path and request/response shape
expectations.evidence: §4 SQL DDL with types (e.g. 'quantity numeric(10,3) null', 'area text not null check (...)'); §6 API table with method & path, body and result, e.g. 'PUT /lines/{id}/ticked | { ticked: boolean, seenQuantity: number|null } | Snapshot; 404 LINE_NOT_FOUND', plus Snapshot/Line shapes.

expectations.text: All written files are in English
expectations.evidence: Design, ADRs 0005–0007 and overview/product/requirements edits are English; German only in UI strings and stakeholder quotes.

expectations.text: Detects the conflict between the stakeholder's 'Sync am besten über Firebase' and the product constraint that FE+BE+DB run on the Pi, and documents it openly (both requirements, resolution, what is lost) instead of silently picking one
expectations.evidence: ADR 0005 lists Firebase vs '001 hard constraint' with cons ('The list database moves off the Pi'); resolution option 2; loss stated in §12: 'The honest trade-off: the list only reaches the store if the phones have the VPN'; Firebase pro 'reachable from the store over mobile data with no network setup'.

expectations.text: The conflict resolution is flagged for later stakeholder confirmation (e.g. a change request for the groomer) without blocking the design
expectations.evidence: §12 'Stakeholder confirmation needed ... Steps 1–5 do not depend on this decision'; overview index 'Firebase/VPN decision pending stakeholder confirmation'. Non-blocking, though routed as a question to the user rather than a change request for the groomer.

expectations.text: Builds on the existing stack (Ktor, PostgreSQL, React PWA, Caddy) without adding a new database or runtime
expectations.evidence: 'No new container. WireGuard runs in the host kernel'; new Ktor module in existing app, tables in existing PostgreSQL, Caddy config, React route. No new DB/runtime.

expectations.text: Addresses that the Pi is currently reachable only in the home network while the list is used in the supermarket over mobile data, and decides how the phone reaches the backend there
expectations.evidence: ADR 0006: 'In the store, the shopper's phone is on mobile data and cannot reach the Pi'; decision self-hosted WireGuard, split tunnel, 'on demand'. (Weakness: requires UDP port forward, CGNAT/DS-Lite risk not discussed; host Pi vs router left open.)

expectations.text: Live updates between household members use a concrete mechanism (e.g. SSE or WebSocket) including reconnect/resync behaviour
expectations.evidence: §6 'GET /events: event: snapshot with the current Snapshot right after connecting, then after every committed change. : ping every 25 s'; §8.3 'EventSource reconnects on its own. Each snapshot event replaces the stored snapshot'; outbox flushed on SSE open.

expectations.text: Offline viewing and ticking: changes are queued locally and replayed; conflicts (e.g. line deleted or shopping finished while offline) have defined outcomes
expectations.evidence: ADR 0007/§8.3: ticks in IndexedDB outbox, flushed on SSE open/online/visibility/30 s; 'A 404 drops the op (the line was deleted or removed by finishing shopping)'; §5.4 split rule for concurrent merges; 'Last write wins between two members'.

expectations.text: Merge rules R1/R2/R2a/R2b are specified precisely (case-insensitive name + same unit, only open recipe lines, quantity-less ingredients, free items never merged)
expectations.evidence: §5.1 name_key lowercase + unit_key; §5.2 'find the open (unticked) RECIPE line with the same name_key and unit_key', 'Not found (including when only ticked lines match, R2a)', quantity-less R2b rule; §5.5 'Always insert a new FREE line, never merged'.

expectations.text: Area assignment is specified: household corrections take priority, then a concrete built-in mapping, fallback Sonstiges; corrections stored household-wide
expectations.evidence: §7: '1. Household correction: exact hit in area_override (R5; takes priority). 2. Built-in dictionary areas-de.tsv ... exact / tk prefix / longest suffix 3. Fallback SONSTIGES'; area_override PK (household_id, name_key); §5.5 'upsert area_override ... (R5, household-wide)'.

expectations.text: The memory/capacity budget of the Pi is re-checked after adding the feature (e.g. long-lived connections)
expectations.evidence: Only restates 'No new container ... Limits stay at 1.34 GB' and ADR 0006 'No change to the container memory budget'. No estimate of memory for held SSE connections/flows or idempotency job; overview.md deployment/budget section not updated. k6 test checks p95 only, not memory.

expectations.text: Asks no questions: the final message contains no question to the user, no options to choose from and no request to review or approve
expectations.evidence: final_message.md contains 'Was ich ohne Rückfrage selbst entschieden habe (bitte prüfen):' and 'Risiken und To-dos vor dem Go-live', and says the business 'muss ... den Auftragsverarbeitungsvertrag (DPA) von OneSignal akzeptieren. Wenn nicht, ersetzen wir OneSignal ...'. It also proposes a spike to settle 'drei Punkte'.

expectations.text: Traceability: every story/acceptance criterion and every business rule of the target requirements document is mapped to a concrete design element
expectations.evidence: §2 maps R1-R12 and S4 one by one to design elements. The S1-S3 acceptance criteria are not listed individually, but each one is covered by a concrete planner rule (§6.1: dueTomorrow, overdue, meisterTasks ==2, status=OPEN / dueDate != null filter, R8 snapshot), and §10 lists one test per acceptance criterion. Checked all ACs: none is left without a design element. This is weaker than an explicit per-AC mapping.

expectations.text: No open decisions: the design contains no TBD/TODO, no 'either X or Y' left to developers, no unresolved 'consider'/'if needed' choices
expectations.evidence: §5: 'The 09:00 cutoff ... is not in the requirement ... Change the constant SEND_WINDOW_END = '09:00' if the stakeholder wants something else.' §11 R2: 'If that is not acceptable, fall back to self-hosted Web Push'. §12: 'Update this design if something fails.' §3: "serviceWorkerPath: 'sw.js' (whatever the generated file is called)". ADR 0005: 'Check this when signing up.'

expectations.text: Out-of-scope items of the target requirements are not designed or built
expectations.evidence: No settings screen ('It is not a settings screen: there is no switch to turn reminders off'), no email fallback, no overdue-only view (/overview reused), no shifting of reminders. The permission-denied hint text and the test-push script are not on the out-of-scope list.

expectations.text: Data model given with entities, fields and types; API/interfaces given with method, path and request/response shape
expectations.evidence: Full Prisma schema for ReminderRun and ReminderMessage with types and constraints (§8). OneSignal 'POST https://api.onesignal.com/notifications' with the full JSON body (§7). Internal interface 'PushSender.send({ messageId, recipientId, heading, body, url }) -> { providerId }'. There are no new Taskli HTTP endpoints because registration goes through external_id. The OneSignal response fields are only named loosely (providerId, recipient count).

expectations.text: All written files are in English
expectations.evidence: The design, ADRs 0005/0006 and the overview.md additions are in English. The German text is limited to push and UI strings, which QE2 requires.

expectations.text: Stays on the existing stack (NestJS/TypeScript, Prisma, PostgreSQL, React PWA) and introduces no new language or database
expectations.evidence: 'New dependency: @nestjs/schedule (v4 ...)'. The web side adds 'react-onesignal'. ADR 0006 rejects Redis/BullMQ. There is no new language or database.

expectations.text: Uses OneSignal for push as the stakeholder stated, including how devices/users are registered (e.g. external user id = Taskli user id)
expectations.evidence: ADR 0005: 'Users are targeted by external_id = User.id'. §3: 'call OneSignal.login(user.id)' after login and on app start, 'OneSignal.logout()' on logout. The send uses 'include_aliases': { 'external_id': [...] }.

expectations.text: The 07:00 trigger is defined in Europe/Berlin although the server runs in UTC, and DST transitions are handled
expectations.evidence: "@Cron('*/5 7-9 * * *', { timeZone: 'Europe/Berlin' })". §5: 'The server runs in UTC ... DST changes are handled by the cron library. Node's bundled ICU contains the tz data'. There is no DST test case, but the handling is defined.

expectations.text: Bavarian holidays are computed per year including Easter-based movable holidays and exclude 15 Aug and 8 Aug
expectations.evidence: §4: fixed dates plus 'Good Friday −2, Easter Monday +1, Ascension +39, Whit Monday +50, Corpus Christi +60' using the Meeus algorithm. 'Explicitly not included: 08-15, 08-08 (a test asserts both are working days)'.

expectations.text: The daily run is idempotent: a restart or duplicate run never sends a second message to a person on the same day (persisted record)
expectations.evidence: ReminderRun is keyed by date and planned once. There is '@@unique([runDate, recipientId])', 'pg_try_advisory_xact_lock', and 'idempotency_key = the message's UUID, so a retry after a timeout never creates a second notification'.

expectations.text: Behaviour after a missed 07:00 run (server down) is defined and consistent with R2/R8
expectations.evidence: The behaviour is defined (catch-up until 09:00), but it is inconsistent. Messages can go out as late as 08:55, and planning happens at that moment, so tasks created after 07:00 are included. Even so, §5 claims 'The plan is the snapshot of the task state at 07:00 (R8)', which is false for catch-up. The design admits 'The 09:00 cutoff ... is not in the requirement'.

expectations.text: Meister notice is sent once per task, persisted, and can re-trigger after a due-date change (R10)
expectations.evidence: §2 R10: 'Notice iff workingDaysOverdue(dueDate, today) == 2; deterministic per due date, so a changed due date re-arms it'. The notice is persisted as a MEISTER_NOTICE ReminderMessage with taskIds. Unit tests cover 'Meister exactly at 2, not at 1 or 3' and 'changed due date re-arms'.

expectations.text: 'Today', 'tomorrow' and working-day overdue counting are computed in Europe/Berlin on date-only due dates
expectations.evidence: 'clock.todayInBerlin()', and 'Dates are YYYY-MM-DD strings (LocalDate), no Date objects'. 'dueDate == today + 1 day'. 'workingDaysOverdue(due, today) = number of working days d with due < d <= today'. ReminderRun.runDate is a 'Berlin local date'.

expectations.text: Tap targets specified: single task opens that task, multiple opens the employee list or the Meister overview
expectations.evidence: §6.4 table: 'Employee or Meister | exactly 1 | /tasks/{id}'; 'Employee | >= 2 | /tasks'; 'Meister | >= 2 | /overview'. The URL is sent as web_url.

notes: Most technical assertions (Kotlin, arm64, wake lock, HTTPS, OneSignal, holidays, DST) pass in both configs: the baseline model already knows the tech. The skill's gains come from process: no questions to the user, no open decisions, full traceability, explicit budgets.
Baseline asked the user/stakeholder to confirm things in all 3 evals ('bitte prüfen', 'muss bestätigen', 'vor Go-live klären') - exactly what the architect must not do.
Both configs detected the Firebase vs Pi conflict; only with_skill wrote a change request and kept the design decided.
with_skill still failed R8 in eval 3: catch-up until 07:59 plans with state at catch-up time, not 07:00.

Not covered by assertions: with_skill eval 1 reorders imported ingredient text (S11 'as written'); with_skill eval 2 lacks idempotency for 'add recipe' retries; with_skill eval 1 adds unrequested scope (password reset, founder role).
Cost: with_skill takes ~2x time (534s vs 271s), mostly on eval 1 (698s).
